purpose: Freeze a zero-founder-cost compute boundary before preregistration, training, or final-split access.
hard_rules: No paid compute, paid API, paid SaaS, or paid accelerator may be required by the Study 1 protocol.
Free accelerator capacity is optional and must never be a single point of failure for protocol completion.
Final evaluation must remain reproducible without purchasing compute.
No final-test labels may be opened or inspected while compute planning is active.
Any experiment that exceeds the frozen compute envelope must be rejected or separately re-governed before execution.

observed_local_host.observation_method: Windows CIM queries executed through the authorized Remote Desktop Commander connection

compute_classes.verified_fact: Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free and unlimited for public repositories; standard Linux and Windows public runners currently expose 4 CPUs, 16 GB RAM, and 14 GB SSD.
Kaggle documents a free NVIDIA Tesla P100 option, while noting that GPU availability is limited and busy periods may place sessions in a queue.
Colab is free, but resource limits and GPU types vary over time and are not guaranteed or published as fixed quotas.

compute_classes.policy: Do not use as qualification evidence or as a required execution path. Promotional credits do not make a paid service a protocol dependency.

assistant_can_execute_without_founder_in: local Windows/WSL commands on the authorized device
GitHub repository work and standard public-repository Actions
requires_founder_owned_login_or_acceptan: credentialed or data-use-agreement datasets such as MIMIC-derived resources
author-issued benchmark credentials such as the full CSEDB verification-prompt path
founder_account_boundaries.rule: Founder interaction may unlock an optional resource, but no ungranted account action may be fabricated or treated as completed.

D2_baseline_qualification.required_compute: local CPU plus public GitHub Actions
D2_baseline_qualification.policy: Qualify simple and matched baselines before architecture expansion.

D3_architecture_candidates.required_compute: local CPU for construction and smoke qualification
D3_architecture_candidates.policy: Reject candidates that cannot support CPU inference or a zero-cost reproducible inference path.

D4_training_objective_experiments.accelerator: optional Kaggle or Colab free tier
D4_training_objective_experiments.policy: Use accelerator time only after a written candidate set and stopping rule exist; do not run open-ended search.

D5_to_D7_development.policy: Calibration, assurance, ablation, and model selection may use only development/calibration evidence and must log every attempted candidate.

D8_protocol_freeze.policy: Bind model/checkpoint digests, environment, seeds, benchmark manifests, metrics, stopping rules, and final-evaluation execution path before final access.

D9_untouched_final_evaluation.accelerator: permitted only if the exact free execution path was frozen before final access and remains available without purchase
D9_untouched_final_evaluation.fallback: If the frozen accelerator path is unavailable, do not substitute paid compute or a different model; record the block and re-govern before any final-label access.

experiment_budget_policy.default_strategy: small candidate grids, fixed seeds, early rejection on development evidence
prohibited: post-hoc expansion after seeing final results
quietly dropping failed or negative trials

protocol_implications: Study 1 must prefer architectures whose inference can run on the founder-controlled CPU host, even if optional free GPU acceleration is used during development.
Public GitHub Actions may qualify software and CPU reproducibility but cannot substitute for scientific independence or final-test sealing.
Kaggle and Colab are convenience accelerators, not availability guarantees.
Any credentialed dataset or account-bound accelerator must have an explicit founder-action boundary before use.
The final benchmark suite and final split remain unfrozen in this compute-plan artifact.
